Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fivenumMeta 0.1.0

  • First release: the functions that accompany the paper of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026), “Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary”.

  • se_imputed_df() takes a meta-analysis data set, one row per study, reads the reporting scenario off the columns each row has, and appends the imputed mean and SD with their naive and exact plug-in standard errors. A row with a sample mean and SD is the scenario "sample", and a row with a mean, the minimum and the maximum and no SD is "mean_range": the mean is kept, and the SD is imputed from the range. For two groups per row, se_imputed_diff() does the same and adds the effect of the study with its naive and its exact standard error, in the names metafor::rma() takes as they are: the difference of means (measure = "MD", the default) or the log variability ratio (measure = "lnVR").

  • pool_imputed() pools the studies of se_imputed_diff() in one call, under the naive and under the exact standard errors side by side, by the common-effect model (method = "EE", the default) or the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model ("DL"): the pooled estimate, its standard error, confidence interval and p-value, Q, I^2, tau^2 and the weights. REML and the other estimators stay with metafor, which takes the same columns.

  • se_imputed() returns one study’s imputed mean and SD with their plug-in standard errors, as an object of class "se_imputed": a list with a compact print. A row of se_imputed_df() whose standard errors would be zero (a sample SD of zero, a summary whose values are all equal) gets NA and is named in the warning with the other rows that cannot be used.

  • c_mu(), c_sigma() and inflation_factors() give the exact factors at every sample size: a reported quantile is a fixed combination of two neighboring order statistics under the definition type (1 to 9 as in quantile(), default 7). So its moments, the estimators and their factors are exact at any n. c_mu_shortcut() and c_sigma_shortcut() give the closed-form shortcut formulas, for comparison and for use without the package.

  • Every function defaults to the BLUE: version = "blue" in the study-level functions and inflation_factors(), method = "blue" in the others. version = "wan_luo_shi" and the method presets give the estimators of Wan, Luo and Shi, exact at every sample size as well.

  • estimator_weights(), scenario_ranks() and imputed_moments() give the weights, the reported ranks and the second moments of the imputed statistics.

  • The exact moments of the normal order statistics come from the package osmoments.

  • The data set vitd carries the six studies of the vitamin D meta-analysis of Nnoaham and Clarke (2008), and the vignette two-meta-analyses reproduces the two meta-analyses of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026), one of means on vitd and one of SDs on metamedian::dat.age.
